problem: Changing the caption translation mode set a cancellation flag but deferred acceptance of the obsolete worker stop until a watchdog poll. The existing watchdog was already bounded; this was not an uncancelled full-generation claim.

observed_red.observation: Actual update_preferences(off) during a TERM-ignoring SSE child: cancellation flag true, owned stop not yet accepted.

changes: After successfully saving and publishing preferences, a changed translation mode synchronously requests the registered worker stop only while translation_busy remains true.
The status lock orders mode changes against the translation-to-minutes handoff; the configuration gate blocks unrelated new task admission. The preference lock is released before signalling.
The existing owned PID/StopState closing and one-stop gate is reused. No pool invalidation, synchronous reap, new epoch, new model invocation or platform-specific stop policy.

validation.regression: Passed: bilingual to off, bilingual to zh-en, unchanged bilingual, and independent minutes. Each observes the real preference entry before cleanup, with actual child/SSE content.
validation.rust_format: passed after formatting the new test tuple
validation.independent_review: No P1/P2 found in final scope; lock ordering, handoff, spawn-after-cancel and stopped-worker reuse reviewed.

limits: Native SSE regression ran on macOS/Unix. It manually drains the existing watchdog stop after acceptance, so it does not measure actual watchdog scheduling latency or Windows native latency.
Actual process exit still uses the existing watchdog and fixed grace/forced-stop mechanism. No measured energy, GPU memory or whole-meeting performance claim.
No new models, GPU components or installers were built. Q9 and Q16 remain open; 0.3.5 remains unreleased.
